problem.explanation: The join groups enrollments per student. HAVING compares each distinct subject count with the total subject count, implementing relational division. A common mistake is COUNT(*) when duplicate enrollments exist. Double NOT EXISTS is a robust alternative.
hints: Count each student's distinct enrolled subjects.
Compare that count with a scalar subquery that counts all subjects.
problem.reference_solution: SELECT s.name FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT e.subject_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM subjects) ORDER BY s.name
problem.statement_markdown: Return students enrolled in every subject currently listed in subjects. Sort student names alphabetically.
problem.title: Students enrolled in all subjects
